block.paragraph: GEOMETRY BASIS — Cap and wind datums derive from the selected Type F pad, 6-in pedestal and 36-in cap. Individual seat grades, separate plates, the retained wind envelope, terrain reference and gross pier-face width require final-detail confirmation.

Service IV is not used in the current nonprestressed pier / steel-pile load set. No Service IV pressure, uplift, or FBMP entry case is produced. Strength III deck uplift remains included.

For girder bridges, wind load components on the substructure are determined as the product of skew coefficients ( LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.3a-1 ), the wind pressure from Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-1 , and the depth of the bridge as seen in elevation perpendicular to the longitudinal axis. Both transverse and longitudinal components are applied simultaneously at mid-depth of the superstructure ( LRFD Art. 3.8.1.2.3a ).

For usual girder and slab bridges with individual span length not more than 150 ft and maximum height not more than 33.0 ft above low ground or water level, simplified wind load components may be used per LRFD Art. 3.8.1.2.3a : Transverse = 100% of perpendicular load; Longitudinal = 25% of transverse load.

textcell.name: C001VerticalScope3
textcell.paragraph: • These cases use wind perpendicular to the bridge. Both transverse signs are evaluated with the matching horizontal load. The selected skew-angle cases elsewhere in C001 remain separate.

block.paragraph: The load-generation table precedes combination factors. Apply the matching factors once in C004. Vertical wind is excluded from other limit states and from skew-wind cases.
Reference: Primary code excerpt: LRFD 3.8.2, 10th Edition (2024)
C001 generates the vertical line loads and windward eccentricity. C004 combines them with gravity and perpendicular horizontal wind for the bearing-contact and overturning checks.
